action_history.rationale: Model: Sum of 3 pseudo-Voigt components + constant baseline offset (no ALS; RRUFF background-subtracted data sits near zero)

result.detailed_analysis: The spectrum is unambiguously diamond. The fitted first-order band at 1336.05 +/- 0.01 cm^-1 with FWHM 14.06 +/- 0.04 cm^-1 corresponds to the triply-degenerate T2g zone-center optical phonon of cubic diamond (nominal 1332 cm^-1). The ~4 cm^-1 upward offset from the canonical 1332 value is within instrumental/calibration tolerance for a 780 nm-excited RRUFF measurement and should not be over-interpreted as strain without calibration verification. The reported FWHM is somewhat broadened by the fit's inability to track the sharp discrete apex (the residual shows +/-320-sigma coherent oscillation across 1305-1360, a classic under-sampling/under-resolution signature of a peak whose intrinsic width approaches the point spacing), so the true intrinsic linewidth is likely equal to or narrower than 14 cm^-1. The eta ~0.61 indicates a mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian character, consistent with an intrinsically Lorentzian phonon convolved with a Gaussian instrument function. The weak broad band at ~2443 cm^-1 (relative intensity 0.003) is the diamond second-order/overtone (2-phonon) scattering, appearing near twice the fundamental; its parameters are poorly constrained (FWHM pinned at the 300 cm^-1 bound, eta pinned at 1.0, center_err 17 cm^-1) so its position and width are only qualitatively meaningful. Component 3 at ~780 cm^-1 (FWHM pinned at 400, eta ~0, large fractional errors, fit dips negative near 1050) is a fitting artifact tracking baseline noise and should NOT be reported as a real spectral feature - no diamond band exists there. Band summary (center cm^-1 / relative intensity, strongest first): 1336 / 1.0 (T2g first-order, real, dominant); 2443 / 0.003 (second-order overtone, real, weakly constrained); 780 / 0.001 (SPURIOUS - reject). Element consistency: ideal chemistry C only; diamond assignment is fully consistent, no conflicting elements.

scientific_claims.claim: The sample exhibits a single dominant first-order Raman band at 1336.05 +/- 0.01 cm^-1 (FWHM 14.06 +/- 0.04 cm^-1, eta ~0.61), identifying it unambiguously as diamond (sp3 carbon, T2g zone-center optical phonon), with a weak second-order band near ~2443 cm^-1 at ~0.3% relative intensity.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: The sharp, single 1332-region T2g line is the definitive Raman fingerprint of crystalline diamond and confirms high crystalline order; the presence of the second-order overtone at roughly twice the fundamental corroborates the assignment and reflects the two-phonon density of states.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone characterized the first-order T2g phonon position and linewidth of natural diamond by Raman spectroscopy and related the linewidth to crystalline quality and phonon lifetime?

issues.problem: The dominant peak is systematically misfit at its apex and flanks — the single pseudo-Voigt cannot reproduce the sharp core plus the observed shoulder structure. Residuals oscillate with several sign-changes (RMS/noise=304–324×) — a coherent under-resolution signature, not counting-statistics scatter on a bright peak.

issues.location: peak_3 (center 780, fwhm≈400) and the modelled bump near 700–900
issues.problem: Component 3 (orange) fits a broad hump at ~780 where the raw data shows only weak, noisy structure near baseline; the fit red curve even dips negative (~-2) near 1050, tracking noise rather than a real band.

This broad component tracks the real ~2450 D-band-like hump adequately (band-2 zoom shows only mild ±5σ structure), but fwhm is pinned exactly at the 300 bound with eta pinned at 1.0 — parameters at bounds indicate incomplete convergence.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add/re-seed a narrow component near x≈1350 to capture the main-peak shoulder (reallocating the spurious peak_3), and relax the fwhm/eta bounds pinned on peak_2 and peak_3.

quality_history.judge_reasoning: Both attempts share the same fundamental limitation: the dominant diamond T2g band at ~1336 cm^-1 cannot be reproduced by a single pseudo-Voigt, producing large coherent residuals (±200-400σ) at the apex/flanks. This is an under-resolution artifact of the peak core, not a global failure, and affects both fits similarly. The distinguishing factor is the treatment of the third component and the sharp-core handling. In Attempt 2, component 3 (orange) degenerates into a physically absurd near-delta-function spike pinned at 1336 (a numerical artifact trying to patch the sharp core), which is clearly nonphysical and not a real spectral band. In Attempt 1, component 3 is a broad band near ~780 cm^-1 that at least attempts to describe the weak low-frequency hump in the data, and although its flanks are somewhat overextended (causing the model to dip slightly negative near 1050), the components remain physically interpretable as diamond first-order (1336), second-order/overtone (~2465), and a broad low-frequency feature. The second-order band region (band 2 zoom) is fit comparably well in both (±5-6σ mild systematic waviness). Given equal global R² (0.9974 vs 0.9980) and equal main-peak deficiency, Attempt 1 is preferred because its components are all physically plausible bands, whereas Attempt 2 contains a spurious delta-spike component that is a fitting artifact rather than a genuine feature.
